questions.question: BUG-280 scope? Orient verdicts: RFC-0017's kernel would remove this defect, but Local only moves onto the kernel at D3 step 5, after four other steps that haven't started, so an in-place fix is right now. BUG-257/255 constrain the fix: spec 003 treats a listing that silently truncates on a failed sub-walk as a defect, and I measured that Local's recursive list_files (rglob and os.walk branches), glob and get_folder_info all silently drop a denied subfolder.

options.label: Three methods, all branches (Recommended)
options.description: Fix list_files (flat + both recursive branches), list_folders and iter_children: a denial anywhere in the walk raises PermissionDenied with path/backend, matching S3Boto3's propagate shape. glob and get_folder_info silent truncation is filed as a new BUG item. The cross-backend pattern is left to RFC-0017 (BK-389 onward).

options.label: Three methods + glob + folder_info
options.description: Also make glob and get_folder_info raise on a denied subtree. Wider: glob needs its own walker in place of Path.glob, and get_folder_info changes from a partial count to an error. Bigger diff and more behaviour change in one PR.

options.label: As filed: top-level iterdir only
options.description: Map the PermissionError from the non-recursive iterdir loops only. Smallest diff, but list_files(recursive=True) keeps answering a denial with a truncated listing, which the spec calls a defect. I'd file that as a separate item.

options.label: Wait for RFC-0017 step 5
options.description: Do nothing now; the kernel's choke point fixes it when Local migrates. That is after v0.33.0 and steps 1 to 4, so the leak stays shipped for several releases.

questions.question: Where should the rule "a denial anywhere in a recursive walk raises PermissionDenied instead of leaving out the denied subtree" be recorded? Today BE-021's ACL row requires PermissionDenied for a denied operation, but nothing says how a recursive listing treats a denied subfolder.

options.label: Local docstrings only (Recommended)
options.description: Put Raises: PermissionDenied on LocalBackend's three listings and say a denied subfolder raises. No spec 003 change. The cross-backend question (does SFTP/Graph/etc. skip or raise?) goes into the new follow-up item with the glob/get_folder_info truncation, so this PR makes no claim about backends it doesn't measure.

options.label: Add a BE-021 clause
options.description: State it in spec 003 for every backend now. That claim binds backends this PR doesn't touch, so the PR would also have to measure SFTP, Graph, Azure HNS and the rest, and record any that disagree as known divergences. Much wider.

questions.question: Where should the rule "a denial anywhere in a recursive walk raises PermissionDenied instead of leaving out the denied subtree" be recorded? Today BE-021's ACL row requires PermissionDenied for a denied operation, but nothing says how a recursive listing treats a denied subfolder.

File this follow-up as BUG-318 (next safe ID per `gen-backlogid --check --remote`) in § 1, where BUG-280 sits now?

BUG-318 — `LocalBackend.glob` and `get_folder_info` leave out a subtree they cannot read
spec: BE-021 · effort: S · audience: user.api
`glob` walks with `Path.glob` and `get_folder_info` with `rglob`, and both swallow every `OSError` from a subfolder scan. A denied subfolder drops out, so the matches, or the file count and size, come back short and read as complete. BUG-280 fixed the three listings with a mapped walk. Open decision: whether BE-021 states for every backend that a recursive walk raises on a denied subtree; no other backend was measured.

options.label: File as drafted (Recommended)
options.description: Index entry only, no dossier: it fits in eight lines, and the measurement is in this PR's trace (orient evidence) and the probe.

options.label: File, glob/folder_info only
options.description: Drop the cross-backend clause question from the item and leave it unrecorded.

options.label: Don't file
options.description: Leave the glob/get_folder_info truncation untracked. The trace still records the measurement.

questions.question: This branch sits on master plus the /ship variant commit fba0850 ("never merge"). How should the PR handle it?

options.label: Push without the variant (Recommended)
options.description: Push a branch rebased onto origin/master, so the PR diff is BUG-280 only. The local worktree keeps the variant commit underneath, so `/ship resume` still reads the variant SKILL.md. Each fix-pass push repeats the rebase (cherry-pick of my commits onto master).

options.label: Push with the variant
options.description: Simplest mechanics. The PR then contains the variant's SKILL.md change, which reviewers see as part of BUG-280, and it has to be dropped before merge.
